resultJson.description:
Slice 2 of 4 of #8 (ADR `docs/adr/0001-adr-start-spotify-from-spotify-refresh-token-fall.md`). Today the code from the callback reaches `SpotifyClient` through one `Deferred`, wrapped by `SignInCodes.once`. Once that Deferred is completed it stays completed. After a failed code exchange (an expired code, a double click, a 5xx), every later poll exchanges the same dead code again until the app is restarted. Slice 4 removes the sp_dc cookie, which leaves the browser as the only fallback, so the browser sign-in has to be retryable.

This epic adds `SignInCodes.make`, which holds at most one pending attempt. `attempt` joins the pending attempt or opens a fresh one. `hand` completes the pending attempt and spends it, or returns false and drops the code when nothing is waiting. `hand` is uncancelable, so a code is never lost between clearing the slot and completing the wait. `SpotifyClient.resource` switches from `Deferred` + `once` to `make`. `initialAuth` opens its attempt before it logs `Please visit:` and before the still-present cookie `GET /authorize`. The order matters. `HttpClients` wraps the Spotify client in `FollowRedirect(2)`, so with a valid sp_dc the callback (and `hand`) runs during the Authorize request itself. With `make`, an attempt opened after that request would miss the code, and the poll would wait forever. Once this is in, a failed exchange fails only that poll. The next poll logs a new URL and waits for a new code, and approving that URL completes sign-in without a restart.

Out of scope for this slice, and left as is: the `/authorize` request with the sp_dc cookie (slice 4 removes it), the startup refresh-token swap and `signIn` (slice 3), and the existing `Deferred` constructor overload (it stays, so every existing test compiles and passes unchanged). There are no deviations from the ADR's program design. The ADR sketches a `callbackRoutes(deferred: Deferred)` overload, but the code has none, and the existing callback test already calls `callbackRoutes[IO](SignInCodes.once(code))`, so none is added.

tasks.title: Add SignInCodes.make: one pending attempt, a spent attempt is replaced
tasks.description:
In `src/main/scala/client/SignInCodes.scala`, add `def make[F[_]: Concurrent]: F[SignInCodes[F]]` as in the ADR (import `cats.effect.Concurrent`). Shape: the state is a `Ref[F, Option[Deferred[F, String]]]` holding the pending attempt.
- `attempt`: allocate a `Deferred` `d`, then `ref.modify { case Some(p) => (Some(p), p.get); case None => (Some(d), d.get) }`. A pending attempt is joined; otherwise the fresh one is installed.
- `hand(code)`: `ref.modify { case Some(p) => (None, p.complete(code)); case None => (None, false.pure[F]) }.flatten`, made **uncancelable** (e.g. `Concurrent[F].uncancelable(_ => ...)`). `hand` runs inside an http4s route that a client disconnect can cancel. A cancel between the modify and the complete would clear the slot without completing `p`, and the waiting poll would then hang forever.

Handing clears the slot, which spends the attempt, so the next `attempt` opens a new one. Leave `once` and the trait docs as they are. Use brace syntax.

Tests go in `src/test/scala/client/SignInCodesSpec.scala`. Keep the three existing `once` tests unchanged and add ScalaCheck properties for `make`:
- A hand before any attempt gives false.
- One code per attempt: each attempt's wait yields exactly the first code handed after it opened, and later hands give false until a new attempt opens.
- A spent attempt is never reused: an attempt opened after a hand waits for the next hand and never yields the earlier code.

Generate random sequences of `Attempt` / `Hand(code)` ops and check them against a tiny pure model. The model holds a pending id or none: an attempt joins or creates, and a hand completes and clears, or returns false. Compare the hand booleans. For each attempt's wait, check that it yields the code the model expects, or is still waiting. Check still waiting with `wait.timeout(1.second)` under `TestControl.executeEmbed`, as the existing test does. The suite is a `CatsEffectSuite`, so either mix in `munit.ScalaCheckSuite` or put the properties in a sibling `ScalaCheckSuite` that runs IO with `unsafeRunSync()` (precedent: `SpotifyRenewSpec`). Name each test by what it checks, with no explanatory comments. Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`.

tasks.title: Retry a failed browser sign-in: open the attempt before logging and /authorize, build SignInCodes.make in resource
tasks.description:
In `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala`:
1. In `initialAuth`, open the attempt first and await it later. Today the order is: log `Please visit`, GET /authorize with the cookie, then `codes.attempt.flatten`. Change it to: `waitForCode <- codes.attempt`, then the log, then the unchanged /authorize request, then `code <- waitForCode`. Do not remove the /authorize request or the cookie (slice 4 does that), and change nothing else in the method.
2. In `SpotifyClient.resource`, replace `Resource.eval(Deferred[F, String]).map(SignInCodes.once[F])` with `Resource.eval(SignInCodes.make[F])`.

`callbackRoutes(codes)` already does `codes.hand(code) *> Ok(...)`, so a false result (nothing waiting) already answers the same page and drops the code. Keep that as is, and don't add a Deferred overload of `callbackRoutes`.

Log capture: `src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` sets `<root level="WARN">`, and `Please visit` is INFO, so it never reaches an appender. Add a test helper to `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala`, next to `capturedLogs`, e.g. `def loggingAt(name: String, level: Level): Resource[IO, Unit]`. It uses `Resource.make` to set the logback `Logger` for `name` to `level` and restore the previous level (possibly null) on release. Use it with `"client.SpotifyClient"` and `Level.INFO`. Don't change logback-test.xml.

Tests go in `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala`; leave the existing tests untouched. Every hand in the tests below comes after a deterministic `IO.sleep` under `TestControl.executeEmbed` that lets the polls block on their attempt. Without it, a hand can run before the forked poll has opened its attempt, the code is dropped, and the test fails with non-termination.

(a) Retry test.
- Setup: `codes <- SignInCodes.make[IO]`, `routes = SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes[IO](codes).orNotFound`, and `new SpotifyClient[IO](Client.fromHttpApp(fake), SpotifyCredentials(<unique client id, e.g. "retry-sign-in">, "secret"), sessionRef(None), codes)`, which is the primary constructor taking SignInCodes.
- The fake: GET /authorize answers `Ok("login")` and hands nothing. POST /api/token records the form's `code` in a Ref, and answers `BadRequest("""{ "error": "invalid_grant" }""")` for `bad-code` (it must be JSON) and `renewedTo("signed-in", Some("refresh-9"))` for `code-2`. GET /v1/me/player answers `Ok(playing)` for bearer `signed-in` and `rejected` otherwise.
- Flow: start poll 1 in a fiber and sleep. Hand `bad-code` via `routes.run(GET /callback?code=bad-code)`, then assert that the join fails with RuntimeException and the session is still None. Start poll 2 in a fiber that records its completion, and sleep. Assert that it hasn't finished and that the token endpoint has seen only `List("bad-code")`. Hand `code-2` via /callback and join. Assert that playback `isPlaying`, the codes are `List("bad-code", "code-2")`, and exactly two `Please visit` events were logged.
- Wrapping: run the flow inside `TestControl.executeEmbed`, wrapped in `Tls.capturedLogs` plus the new INFO-level resource. Filter `Tls.logged(appender)` on `getLoggerName == "client.SpotifyClient"` and a message containing the unique client id, because suites run in parallel and the appender is on the root logger. `Slf4jLogger` logs synchronously inside `IO`, so this works under TestControl.

(b) Hand during /authorize (pins the reorder). With `codes <- SignInCodes.make[IO]`, the fake GET /authorize does `codes.hand("code-1") *> Ok("signed in")`, which simulates the sp_dc redirect landing on the callback. POST /api/token answers `renewedTo("signed-in", Some("refresh-9"))`, and /v1/me/player is as above. Assert that `getPlaybackState` returns playing. Run it under `TestControl.executeEmbed`, or with a `.timeout`, so that without the reorder it fails instead of hanging.

(c) No sign-in waiting. With `SignInCodes.make[IO]`, `/callback?code=dropped` answers `Status.Ok` with the body `Success! Return to your terminal.`. A later `codes.attempt` wait does not yield `dropped`: it times out under `TestControl.executeEmbed`.

Docs:
- `docs/how-it-works.md` §1: change the diagram line `CB->>App: complete Deferred with the code` to say the callback hands the code to the waiting sign-in. Add one bullet: a failed code exchange fails that poll, the next poll logs a new URL to approve, and no restart is needed.
- `docs/architecture.md` (around line 300): change the `Deferred` bullet to name `SignInCodes` (one code per sign-in attempt).
- Don't touch the sp_dc text (slice 4).

Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`. Confirm that the existing SpotifyClientSpec, SpotifyTlsSpec, SpotifyTlsEngineSpec and SignInCodesSpec tests pass unchanged.

resultJson.brief:
Project: a Scala 3 app that syncs Spotify playback to Hue lights. sbt build. Typelevel stack: Cats Effect 3, fs2, http4s Ember, circe, log4cats-slf4j over logback, munit + munit-scalacheck + munit-cats-effect 2.0.0.

Conventions (read CLAUDE.md):
- New code uses brace syntax and `given`/`using`.
- Errors are typed.
- No `unsafeRun*` in main code. Tests do use `unsafeRunSync` in ScalaCheckSuites, e.g. SpotifyRenewSpec.
- Make minimal changes at the point of the problem.
- Comment only what the code can't say.
- Test names say what they check, with no explanatory comments.
- Finish with `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`: lint plus tests with coverage, failing below 90% statements or 85% branches overall, or 70% statements per file. Never lower the thresholds or widen the exclusions.
- Never print or read `.env`.

Design source: `docs/adr/0001-adr-start-spotify-from-spotify-refresh-token-fall.md` (Program design + Slices). This work is slice 2. Slice 1 is already merged, with one deviation from the ADR: `SpotifyCredentials.refreshToken` is `Option[String] = None` (not `String = \"\"`), and `configuredRefreshToken = refreshToken.map(_.trim).filter(_.nonEmpty)`. Tests build credentials as `SpotifyCredentials(\"id\", \"secret\", Some(\"refresh\"))`, or with two args for none. The ADR sketches a `callbackRoutes(deferred: Deferred)` overload, but none exists in the code and none is needed. The existing callback test calls `callbackRoutes[IO](SignInCodes.once(code))`.

Key files:
- `src/main/scala/client/SignInCodes.scala`
  - `trait SignInCodes[F[_]] { def attempt: F[F[String]]; def hand(code: String): F[Boolean] }`.
  - `object SignInCodes { def once[F[_]: Applicative](deferred: Deferred[F, String]): SignInCodes[F] }` exists: attempt = `deferred.get.pure`, hand = `deferred.complete`. `once` returns true for a hand before any attempt.
  - `make[F[_]: Concurrent]: F[SignInCodes[F]]` is to be added here.
- `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala` (the existing code uses colon/indent style; match it when editing these lines)
  - Class: `SpotifyClient[F[_]: Async: Network](client: Client[F], creds: SpotifyCredentials, session: Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]], codes: SignInCodes[F])`, plus an auxiliary constructor taking `authCode: Deferred[F, String]` (wraps it with `once`).
  - `initialAuth` (lines 66-100):
    - builds `authUrl` with `client_id=${creds.clientId}` and redirect `http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback`
    - logs INFO `Please visit: $authUrl`
    - does a `naming(\"Authorize\")` GET of the authorize URL with the `Cookie: sp_dc=...` header (stays until slice 4)
    - then `code <- codes.attempt.flatten`
    - POSTs `grant_type=authorization_code` to `https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token` under `naming(\"Code Exchange\")`; on error it decodes the body `as[Json]`, logs ERROR `Spotify Exchange Failed. Body:` and raises a RuntimeException
    - requires `resp.refresh_token`, then stores the `SpotifySession`
  - `getOrRefresh`: a `None` session → `initialAuth`.
  - `renew`: a `None` session → `configuredRefreshToken.fold(initialAuth)(refreshWith(\"Renew\", _))`.
  - Companion:
    - `callbackRoutes[F[_]: Async](codes: SignInCodes[F])`: `GET /callback?code=` → `codes.hand(code) *> Ok(\"Success! Return to your terminal.\")`; no `code` → 404.
    - `serverResource(codes)` binds 127.0.0.1:7070.
    - `resource(client, creds)` currently builds `Deferred` + `SignInCodes.once`.
    - `CodeMatcher` is a `QueryParamDecoderMatcher(\"code\")`.
  - The logger is `Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]`, logger name `client.SpotifyClient`.
- `src/main/scala/client/HttpClients.scala:22`: the Spotify client is `FollowRedirect(2)`. In production, a valid sp_dc makes `GET /authorize` redirect to the local callback, so `hand` runs during the Authorize request. The attempt must therefore be open before that request.
- `src/main/scala/domain/spotify/SpotifyCredentials.scala`; `SpotifySession(accessToken, refreshToken)`.
- Tests:
  - `src/test/scala/client/SignInCodesSpec.scala`: CatsEffectSuite with three `once` tests. It uses `TestControl.executeEmbed(... .timeout(1.second).attempt)` to show a wait doesn't complete.
  - `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala`: CatsEffectSuite. It fakes Spotify with `Client.fromHttpApp(HttpRoutes.of[IO]{...}.orNotFound)`. Helpers: the `playing` JSON, `rejected` (401), and `renewedTo(access, refresh: Option[String])` token JSON. The existing sign-in tests fake `GET /authorize` completing the Deferred.
  - `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTlsSpec.scala` and `src/test/scala/SpotifyTlsEngineSpec.scala` use the Deferred constructor and expect the call name \"Authorize\". They must keep passing unchanged.
  - `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyRenewSpec.scala` and `SpotifyTokenErrorSpec.scala` show the ScalaCheckSuite + `forAll` + Gen style.
  - `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala`: `Tls.capturedLogs: Resource[IO, ListAppender[ILoggingEvent]]` is attached to the root logger, so filter by logger name and a unique client_id, because suites run in parallel. `Tls.logged(appender): List[ILoggingEvent]` exposes `getLoggerName`, `getFormattedMessage` and `getLevel`. Logback classes: `ch.qos.logback.classic.{Logger, Level}`; get a logger with `LoggerFactory.getLogger(name).asInstanceOf[Logger]`.
  - `src/test/resources/logback-test.xml`: the root level is WARN.
- Docs:
  - `docs/how-it-works.md` §1: the sequence diagram's line 18 says `complete Deferred with the code`; the bullets are at lines 24-27.
  - `docs/architecture.md` ~line 300: `Deferred` to hand the OAuth code.
  - Leave the sp_dc mentions alone (slice 4) and leave README alone (slice 3).

Non-obvious points:
- INFO logs (`Please visit`) are filtered out in tests by the WARN root level in logback-test.xml. Every existing log assertion checks WARN or ERROR. To assert on INFO, raise the `client.SpotifyClient` logger to INFO for the test with a Resource that restores the previous level.
- `Slf4jLogger` logs synchronously inside `IO`, so log capture works under `TestControl`.
- The `/authorize` request still runs in this slice, so any fake used with `initialAuth` must answer GET /authorize. Otherwise the poll fails on a 404 before it waits.
- `initialAuth` decodes error bodies as Json, so fakes should return JSON error bodies.
- With `make`, a hand that arrives when no attempt is open is dropped. In tests, every hand must come after the polling fiber has opened its attempt: under TestControl, sleep first so the fibers block. `.start` alone doesn't guarantee the forked fiber has run.
- `callbackRoutes` ignores the Boolean from `hand`, and that is intended: the same page either way.
- `hand` must be uncancelable. A cancelled route between clearing the slot and completing the Deferred would leave a poll waiting forever, because waits never time out.
